_comment: VERSIONED CORRECTION OF r3. THE CRITERIA ARE AGAIN BYTE-IDENTICAL.
r1, r2 and r3 are preserved unchanged, as are the verdicts produced under them. None is
reopened.
r3 said its roles map deliberately names more files than any one bundle carries, so that
supplying MORE of the implementation would not require another version. It did not name
enough: the repairs the r3 round asked for produced a new test file, and a file with no
role arrives as context, and context cannot be evidence.
r4 adds roles for that file and for every other file the repository could plausibly supply
to one of these three reviews, so that this reason for a new version does not recur. It
changes no criterion, no review_object, no out_of_scope and no verdict_must_state.
The r3 comment follows, unchanged:
VERSIONED CORRECTION OF r2. THE CRITERIA ARE AGAIN BYTE-IDENTICAL.
r1 and r2 are preserved unchanged, as are the verdicts produced under them
(ALPHA-R2-TENANCY-0002 BLOCK, ALPHA-R2-TENANCY-0003 BLOCK). Neither is reopened.
The r2 round returned three PASS, three NOT_EVIDENCED and one FAIL, and the reasons were
fair: the bundle did not contain the adapters for every door, did not contain the counter
implementation, and the counter-checks covered selected mechanisms rather than each
property. Those gaps were closed by writing code and tests -- a door-level isolation suite,
an account usage figure, and six more counter-checks -- and by putting the files a reviewer
asked for into the bundle.
r3 exists only because a file that is not in the roles map arrives as context, and context
cannot be evidence. It assigns roles to the files that were added. It changes no criterion,
no review_object, no out_of_scope and no verdict_must_state; a diff touches the _comment
and the roles map and nothing else. The roles map deliberately names more files than any
one bundle carries, so that supplying a reviewer with MORE of the implementation never
again requires a new profile version.
The r2 comment follows, unchanged:
VERSIONED CORRECTION OF alpha-r2-<slice>-r1. THE CRITERIA ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL.
r1 was frozen prospectively and is preserved unchanged, along with the verdict produced
under it (ALPHA-R2-TENANCY-0002, BLOCK, all seven NOT_EVIDENCED). This does not reopen
that verdict and does not weaken anything.
What r1 got wrong was infrastructure, not judgement. It carries the roles_rule -- 'any
input this profile does not list defaults to the lowest authority, context' -- and then
lists no inputs at all. So every file in the bundle arrived as context, the reviewer
instructions say context cannot substitute for evidence, and EVERY criterion was
necessarily NOT_EVIDENCED whatever the code did. r1 was unsatisfiable by construction.
r2 adds the roles map and changes NOTHING else. Every criterion id, every criterion text,
the review_object, the out_of_scope list and the verdict_must_state are carried over
character for character; a diff of the two files touches only the _comment block and the
new roles section.
The r1 comment follows, unchanged:
TRUSTED REVIEW PROFILE, FROZEN PROSPECTIVELY.
Written and committed BEFORE the code it judges exists. The commit that adds this file
contains no implementation of anything it names. That ordering is checkable in git.
This profile judges ONE sub-contract of Managed Alpha R2: whether this service can hold more
than one customer at a time without either of them being able to see, reach, exhaust or
withdraw anything belonging to the other. It does not judge admission, data retention,
billing or monitoring; those have their own frozen profiles.
A pass concerns this sub-contract only. It is not a finding that the service is fit for the
public, and it is not authorisation to expose anything, release, deploy, take payment, buy a
domain or buy infrastructure. Port 8099 stays closed.
review_object: Multi-tenant accounts for the managed sandbox: the separation of account, person, device, AI connection, sandbox run and operator; how an account comes to exist; how a device, a browser session and an AI connection are attached to exactly one account; and every place where one account's data, credentials, capacity or control surface could become reachable from another account.
out_of_scope: admission, quotas, rate limits and abuse handling, which are judged by alpha-r2-admission-r1
retention, deletion, redaction, export and backup, which are judged by alpha-r2-dataops-r1
public exposure, payment, release, deployment, domains, new infrastructure or new running costs
the kernel-level separation between two accounts' running jobs, which single-host-development does NOT provide and which this profile must not be read as establishing
verdict_must_state: A pass concerns this code, its tests and the measurements presented, and nothing else. On single-host-development two accounts' jobs still run on one kernel: this profile can establish that one account cannot READ, REACH or WITHDRAW another's data and credentials through the service, and cannot establish that one account's job cannot affect another's through the machine. This is not authorisation to expose anything, to deploy, or to charge for it.
roles_rule: Any input this profile does not list defaults to the lowest authority, 'context'. A request may name this profile and may not extend it.

criteria.text: Judge whether every credential, device, browser session, AI connection and run this gateway can hold is attributed to exactly one account, established by the server. Determine whether an account attribution can be absent, empty, duplicated, or supplied by a caller; what the code does when it meets a record from before accounts existed; and whether that migration can place two previously unrelated devices into one account. State what an unattributed record is treated as, and whether that treatment is the permissive or the restrictive one.

Judge, operation by operation and door by door, whether a caller authenticated as account A can obtain anything belonging to account B: a device list, a session list, a run, its status, its result, its output, usage figures, an invitation, an enrolment, a meter line, an audit line, a policy, a ceiling, or the existence of any of those. Determine whether the check is performed in the one dispatcher or repeated per operation; whether an operation added later would be covered by construction or only if somebody remembered; and whether a caller can distinguish 'belongs to another account' from 'does not exist'.

Judge whether a caller in account A can change anything in account B: withdraw or rotate a device, end a session, cancel or submit a run, consume or invalidate an invitation or enrolment ticket, alter a ceiling, or cause a suspension. Determine specifically whether device revocation resolves its target by scanning every credential this gateway holds rather than only the caller's own account, and whether the evidence for each includes an attempt that is refused rather than only an attempt that succeeds for the rightful owner.

Judge whether the operator's surfaces -- the kill switch, ceilings, policy, suspension, retention settings, the metrics and any administrative listing -- are reachable by any account holder over any door, including the browser console, and whether any account-scoped capability can be escalated into an operator one. Determine whether operator authority comes from something an account can never present, and whether an operator action is attributable to an operator rather than to an account.

Judge whether the tool surface offered to an AI can create, join, name, rename, suspend, enumerate or switch accounts, or manage devices, tokens, sessions, invitations or policy in any account including its own. Determine whether this is enforced where a name becomes an operation rather than only where the tool list is built, and whether a newly declared operation is refused by default until classified. State what happens when a model calls a management operation by its exact name.

Judge whether one account's use can consume, reset, corrupt or reveal another's. Determine whether counters, locks, files and identifiers are keyed such that a caller-influenced value cannot collide with or impersonate another account's key; whether a shared counter file is locked across processes; and whether an unreadable counter is read as zero. State what a person in account A can learn about account B's activity from timing, refusals, counters or error text.

Judge the presented tests and counter-checks rather than the claims. For each isolation property, determine whether a test exists that constructs two real accounts and asserts a refusal, rather than asserting a helper returns a filtered list; whether the presented counter-check removes the mechanism and shows a NAMED, DIFFERENT test failing with a non-zero exit; and whether the counter-check proves the revert landed and was restored. A property whose only evidence is a passing test that would also pass without the mechanism is NOT_EVIDENCED.
